experiments.interpretation: In this cache-hot in-process mechanism test, separate stores behind one same-process logical planner matched/slightly beat the monolith while explicit JSON boundaries added about 20.9 us p50 versus the same-process separate-store path. This is not a production benchmark and does not select a universal physical layout.

Both one-engine atomicity and canonical+durable-outbox replay prevented final cross-view mismatch in the constructed family. Unsynchronized direct commits did not. Outbox intentionally tolerates temporary derived lag and repairs it.

Authenticated records alone did not preserve selected membership when unauthenticated structure influenced selection. Re-selection on authenticated structure restored the constructed baseline in all cases. This is a synthetic reproduction of the mechanism class, not an independent replication of Fei et al.'s full system.

This result is deliberately downweighted: the cost surface was constructed rather than measured. It demonstrates that multi-axis placement can express regimes a binary store label cannot, but the fractions are not evidence for real FRANK placement.
JSON converted tuple containers to lists while preserving declared ordered content. Therefore exact emitted representation identity and typed semantic identity must remain distinct.

experiments.kind: real SQLite in-memory write-path mechanism benchmark
experiments.interpretation: The safer replayable outbox path had a real mechanism-local write cost in this test; monolithic one-transaction writes were fastest. UnifiedDB must treat recovery and write latency as a trade-off, not assume the hybrid is free.

Under the chosen synthetic lag distribution, accepting every derived view was unsafe for critical reads while one global exact barrier rejected substantially more operations than an operation-class policy. These rates are not FRANK lag estimates.

negative_results: The first service-equivalence comparator incorrectly treated tuple->list host representation change as semantic query failure; it was corrected with an explicit typed semantic canonicalizer.
Canonical+outbox recovery is not free: it was materially slower than one-engine atomic writes in the in-memory write benchmark.
The placement-lattice winner fractions come from a constructed cost surface and are not eligible as target performance evidence.
No current experiment proves Android performance, production durability, target-Qwen cognition benefit or end-to-end FRANK throughput.
